# Overview

GX helps teams understand and review AI-written code without treating every pull request as an isolated diff.

The open-source `gx` CLI installs Git hooks that capture coding sessions and link them to your commits as reviewable revisions, and adds AI review with `gx review`. You keep using plain Git — `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` — and GX does its work automatically on the way through. The paid GitHub features add [PR Summaries and `@gx` chat](/docs/github) inside GitHub pull requests.

## Start here

- [Get started](/docs/getting-started): install GX, sign in, and publish your first revision.
- [How it works](/docs/how-it-works): why GX stores more context than Git, and what revisions are.
- [CLI](/docs/cli): every command with flags, examples, and exit codes.
- [MCP setup](/docs/mcp): give coding agents review context through the `gx_review` MCP tool.
- [Pull Requests](/docs/github): PR Summaries, `@gx` chat, and paid GitHub review features.
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting): common errors and how to fix them.

## Core workflow

You keep working in plain Git. Once `gx init` installs the hooks, your normal `git` commands do the GX work automatically — there is no GX-specific save verb to learn.

```bash
git add <files>                        # choose the scope of the change
git commit -m "describe this change"   # a hook records it as a GX revision
git push                               # the pre-push hook captures sessions + publishes review context
```

A commit looks like any other:

```text
$ git add src/retry.js
$ git commit -m "add retry helper with attempt limit"
[main b694d3be] add retry helper with attempt limit
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+)
```

Behind that ordinary commit, GX's `prepare-commit-msg` and `post-commit` hooks record a GX **revision** (`qltmnmynnyzk`) — an editable review unit that carries review context: which captured session produced it, and where it sits among your branches. When you `git push`, the pre-push hook links each captured session to the hunks it changed and publishes the review bundle.

GX adds three commands on top of Git — and nothing that duplicates Git itself:

```bash
gx init      # set up hooks and identity in a repo (run once)
gx review    # AI review of your current change, with codebase + session context (alias: gxr)
gx doctor    # check capture, hooks, and workflow state
```

## Product model

GX uses a few terms consistently:

- **Session**: captured coding context from an agent, editor, or shell.
- **Revision**: one reviewable logical change — a Git commit plus the context that explains how it was produced.
- **Stack**: an ordinary Git branch carrying more than one revision — a line of work reviewed together.
- **Review bundle**: the published payload that joins code changes, sessions, metadata, and review evidence.

These are just names for what your ordinary Git commits and branches already are, plus the review context GX records around them. You never leave Git to get them.

A Git commit is a durable snapshot plus a short message. That is still useful, but it is often too thin for AI-generated work: the commit does not know which agent session produced it, which prompt or shell commands mattered, whether the change was split out of a larger messy workspace, or how it relates to nearby generated work.

A GX revision is the review unit: a Git commit plus the review context recorded around it — session provenance, generated summary, file-level intent, and its position on the branch. Calling it a revision keeps the focus on reviewable evolution of the work, not only on the final Git object.

Your branch stays a plain Git branch. GX records the ordered revisions and context around the branch you already have, so reviewers can see the sequence of intent instead of only the final branch state.

# Get started

Start with GX when you want coding agents to produce reviewable work instead of one large undifferentiated diff.

The usual path is:

1. Install the CLI.
2. Sign in with GitHub.
3. Initialize GX in a repository.
4. Stage and commit with Git, review, and push.

## Install

The CLI runs on macOS and Linux (arm64 / amd64):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, run GX inside WSL. You can request a native Windows build from the [download page](/download).

The installer places three binaries in `~/.local/bin`:

| Binary | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `gx` | the CLI |
| `gx-mcp` | stdio MCP server for coding agents ([MCP setup](/docs/mcp)) |
| `gxr` | shortcut for `gx review` |

Verify the install:

```bash
gx version   # prints the installed version
gx doctor    # checks capture, hooks, and workflow state
```

## Sign in

GX uses GitHub for identity. Cloud sign-in is required to push metadata and use GX code review.

```bash
gx auth login
gx auth status
```

The web app sign-in and CLI sign-in are linked through your GitHub account. After signing in from the CLI, you can see signed-in CLI devices in the web app, including machine name, GX version, last-used time, and session expiry. Pass `--name` to control how the machine appears there:

```bash
gx auth login --name "work-laptop"
```

Log out with:

```bash
gx auth logout
```

## Initialize a repo

Run `gx init` once, from the repository you want GX to manage:

```text
$ gx init

Configured     gx identity as Ada Doc <ada@example.com>
Git hooks      ok: record on commit, capture on git push
Claude hooks   ok: Stop/SessionEnd transcript capture
MCP            ok: claude
AGENTS.md      ok: added GX workflow instructions

Next           git add <files> && git commit -m "..."
```

Line by line:

- **gx identity** — the name and email recorded on GX revisions. Defaults to your Git identity; override with `gx init --name "..." --email "..."`.
- **Git hooks** — `prepare-commit-msg` and `post-commit` record each `git commit` as a GX revision, and a `pre-push` hook captures sessions and publishes GX metadata when you `git push`.
- **Claude hooks** — Claude Code `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hooks, so agent transcripts are captured as GX sessions.
- **MCP** — registers the [GX MCP server](/docs/mcp) with supported agent CLIs found on the machine.
- **AGENTS.md** — offers to append GX workflow instructions telling agents working in this repo to use plain Git (GX's hooks record the revision).

For scripts and agent sandboxes, `gx init -y` accepts all defaults and suppresses interactive prompts.

To skip the per-repository step entirely, `gx init --global` installs the hooks once for every repository on the machine — useful when you don't want to remember `gx init` in a new clone. See [CLI → Machine-wide hooks](/docs/cli#machine-wide-hooks).

## Optional: bring your own model key

You do not need a model API key to use GX. The core workflow is fully deterministic, and once you sign in, AI features like `gx review` run through GX Cloud on your plan or free trial.

Set your own key only when you want GX to call a specific provider or model directly:

```bash
gx set key                                              # interactive: pick provider, paste key
gx set key --provider anthropic --key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"   # scripts
```

GX looks for an existing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment first, and stores a pasted key in `~/.gx/inference.json` (or `$GX_HOME/inference.json`). When both are available, your own key takes precedence over GX Cloud.

Paid pull request features (PR Summaries, `@gx` chat) always run through GX Cloud, never your local keys.

## First revision

After making changes, stage the files that belong together and commit them with plain Git:

```text
$ git add src/retry.js
$ git commit -m "add retry helper with attempt limit"
[main b694d3be] add retry helper with attempt limit
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+)
```

What happened:

- `git add` chose the scope — only `src/retry.js` is part of this revision. Use `git add -p` to select individual hunks.
- `git commit` landed the change on the current branch as usual. Behind it, GX's `prepare-commit-msg` and `post-commit` hooks recorded a GX revision (`qltmnmynnyzk`) that carries the review context around the commit.
- Because no coding session was captured for this commit, the revision's provenance is `absent`. When an agent session is captured, GX matches it automatically and links it instead.

Then publish:

```bash
git status   # inspect first
git push     # the GX pre-push hook captures sessions and publishes metadata
```

`git push` pushes normal Git refs; with the GX hook installed, capture and cloud publish happen on the way out.

## Build a stack

A stack is just an ordinary Git branch with more than one commit on it. Start a branch for a line of work, then keep committing to grow it:

```text
$ git checkout -b feature/retry-backoff
Switched to a new branch 'feature/retry-backoff'

$ git add src/backoff.js
$ git commit -m "add exponential backoff helper"
[feature/retry-backoff 14c101a1] add exponential backoff helper
 1 file changed, 18 insertions(+)

$ git add src/jitter.js
$ git commit -m "add jitter to backoff delays"
[feature/retry-backoff ae0d5b62] add jitter to backoff delays
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)
```

GX recorded a revision for each commit as it landed. Inspect the stack with plain Git — it is just the branch's own commits, newest first:

```text
$ git log --oneline main..feature/retry-backoff
ae0d5b62 add jitter to backoff delays
14c101a1 add exponential backoff helper
```

The branch `feature/retry-backoff` is the stack: `main` is its base, and each commit on it is a GX revision. When you `git push`, the pre-push hook publishes the whole branch as a reviewable stack.

## Agent workflow

Agents work in plain Git, exactly like you do:

1. Stage with `git add`
2. Commit with `git commit` — GX's hooks record the revision
3. Push with `git push` — the pre-push hook captures sessions and publishes metadata

The MCP server adds one tool worth wiring up: agents can run `gx_review` for review context on the current change.

See [MCP setup](/docs/mcp) for `add-mcp`, Executor, and per-tool parameters.

# How it works

GX adds a context layer around your existing Git workflow. It captures what happened during coding sessions, attaches that context to reviewable revisions, and publishes normal Git branches and commits — so reviewers see the intent behind a change, not just the final diff.

## The problem

Git was built for humans typing commits one at a time. A commit stores a snapshot and a short message, and for human-paced work that is usually enough.

Agent-written code breaks two of Git's assumptions:

1. **The context that explains a change never makes it into the repo.** The prompt that asked for the change, the commands the agent ran, the tests it executed, the dead ends it backed out of — all of that lives in a session transcript that is gone by review time. The commit message is whatever one line survived.
2. **Review is now the bottleneck.** The cost of generating code is dropping toward zero, but teams still review line by line. When a pull request is one large undifferentiated diff with a thin message, the reviewer has to reconstruct intent from scratch.

## What GX captures

GX records work at two levels:

- **Sessions** — transcripts from coding agents (for example, Claude Code transcripts via `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hooks that `gx init` installs). GX stages a lightweight reference locally, and on `git push` publishes the session alongside the code it produced; the published session is kept with your review history in GX Cloud.
- **Revisions** — each plain `git commit` records the staged changes as one reviewable unit via the GX hooks, down to individual [hunks](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Interactive-Staging) (a few changed lines, not whole files). GX links each revision to the session that produced it automatically, by matching the changed hunks against captured session activity — you never attach anything by hand.

Because changes are stored as described hunks with linked sessions, GX can point reviewers at the parts that matter and let them skim the mechanical rest — instead of forcing a line-by-line read of everything.

## Revisions

You already know the Git mental model of branches and commits. GX keeps exactly that model and records review context around it — no new objects to learn.

A **revision** is a Git commit plus the review context GX records around it: the session that produced it, the changed hunks, and a generated summary. Your branch is just a Git branch; GX adds nothing on top of it. Each revision is separately reviewable, and the order of commits on the branch tells the story of the work.

## Everything is still just Git

When you `git push`, the GX pre-push hook publishes:

- normal Git **branches and commits**, so your Git log and GitHub stay standard;
- the linked **sessions and metadata** to GX Cloud as a review bundle.

Nothing about your repository becomes GX-specific. If you stopped using GX tomorrow, your branches and commits remain ordinary Git.

## Your Git workflow, unchanged

You might expect a set of `gx` verbs to learn. There are none for everyday work — after `gx init`, keep using the Git you already know:

```bash
git switch -c feature/my-change        # a normal branch, when you want one
git add <files>                        # choose the scope of the change
git commit -m "describe this change"   # a hook records it as a GX revision
git push                               # the pre-push hook captures sessions + publishes
```

Plain `git commit` records the staged work as a GX revision. Use `git status` to inspect local state and `gx review` (alias `gxr`) to review the current change. Plain `git push` publishes the code plus linked session data and metadata to GitHub and GX Cloud through the pre-push hook.

## Where the context goes

The published review bundle powers the review surfaces:

- [PR Summaries](/docs/github) tell reviewers what changed, why, and which files deserve attention first.
- [`@gx` chat](/docs/github) answers questions inside the pull request, citing the sessions and diffs it used.
- [`gx review`](/docs/cli) runs a local review using the same captured context before you ever open a PR.

The recommended way to give agents review context is through the [MCP server](/docs/mcp): it exposes the `gx_review` tool so your coding tool can review its own work in the loop, without dropping to the terminal.

# CLI

`gx` is the local CLI. It is open source and runs on your machine. It adds a quality and workflow layer around your existing repo instead of replacing GitHub.

You work in plain Git — `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` — and once `gx init` installs the hooks, GX records review context around your commits automatically: which session produced each change, and where it sits in your stack. GX adds a few commands of its own; it does not replace any Git command you already use.

## Core loop

Once `gx init` installs the hooks, you work entirely in plain Git. There is no GX save verb to learn — your normal commands do the GX work on the way through.

```bash
git add <files>                        # choose the scope of the change
git commit -m "describe this change"   # a hook records it as a GX revision
git status                             # inspect state with plain Git
git push                               # the pre-push hook captures sessions and publishes review context
```

A commit looks like any other — GX records the revision behind it without changing Git's output:

```text
$ git add src/retry.js
$ git commit -m "add retry helper with attempt limit"
[main b694d3be] add retry helper with attempt limit
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+)
```

Behind that commit, GX's `prepare-commit-msg` and `post-commit` hooks record a GX **revision** — an editable review unit that carries context: which captured session produced it, and where it sits among your branches. On `git push`, the pre-push hook links each captured session to the hunks it changed and publishes the review bundle that becomes your PR summary.

A revision is a Git commit plus the review context GX records around it; a stack is just the Git branch those revisions sit on. You never leave Git to get them.

Provenance is inferred automatically. GX matches captured sessions to the commit's changed hunks, so the review bundle knows which session produced each change — there is no manual attach step, and agents do not declare provenance by hand.

GX adds a few commands on top of Git — and nothing that duplicates Git itself:

```bash
gx init      # set up hooks and identity in a repo (run once)
gx review    # AI review of your current change, with codebase + session context (alias: gxr)
gx doctor    # check capture, hooks, and workflow state
```

Setup and support commands round out the surface: `gx auth`, `gx set`, and `gx version`.

## gx init

```bash
gx init
```

Prepares the current repository for GX: configures local identity, installs the Git hooks that record each commit as a revision and capture sessions on push (`prepare-commit-msg`, `post-commit`, and `pre-push`), installs Claude Code transcript-capture hooks, registers the MCP server with supported agent CLIs, and offers to add GX workflow instructions to `AGENTS.md`.

Run it once per repository.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | user name to store in GX config (defaults to Git identity) |
| `--email <email>` | user email to store in GX config |
| `-y`, `--yes` | accept defaults and suppress prompts — use in scripts and agent sandboxes |
| `--global` | install the hooks machine-wide instead of for one repository (see below) |

```text
$ gx init

Configured     gx identity as Ada Doc <ada@example.com>
Git hooks      ok: record on commit, capture on git push
Claude hooks   ok: Stop/SessionEnd transcript capture
MCP            ok: claude
AGENTS.md      ok: added GX workflow instructions

Next           git add <files> && git commit -m "..."
```

### Machine-wide hooks

`gx init --global` installs the hooks once for every repository, so you still get
capture and PR summaries in a repo where you forgot to run `gx init`:

```bash
gx init --global
```

It writes the hooks to `~/.gx/hooks` and points Git at them with
`git config --global core.hooksPath`. Because a global hooks path makes Git ignore
each repository's own `.git/hooks`, GX's scripts **chain**: they do GX's work and
then run the repository's own hook of the same name, passing along its arguments,
input, and exit code — so husky, lefthook, and hand-written hooks keep working.

If a global hooks path is already set to something that is not GX's, `gx init --global`
stops and tells you rather than overwriting it.

Exclude a single repository, from inside it:

```bash
git config gx.enabled false
```

Undo the machine-wide install:

```bash
git config --global --unset core.hooksPath
```

`gx doctor` reports whether the machine-wide hooks are installed and healthy.

## gx review

```bash
gx review                                 # alias: gxr
gx review "check auth rollback risks"
```

Reviews your changes using codebase context, captured sessions, review resources, and optional prompt guidance. Findings are printed as markdown and recorded to review history so future reviews can retrieve previous decisions.

AI reviewers are optional and resolve credentials in this order: your own key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `gx set key`), then GX Cloud when you are signed in (on your plan or free trial), then deterministic checks only — the review always completes, with a warning naming what was unavailable.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[prompt]` | optional positional prompt to steer the review |
| `--base <ref>` | review the commit range `<ref>...HEAD` instead of the working tree |
| `--scope <scope>` | focused review scope: `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `--focus <path>` | limit review to files under this path prefix |
| `--deep` | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `--verbose` | include repo facts, docs, and changed files in the output |
| `--json` | print the report as JSON instead of markdown |
| `--fail-on <level>` | exit non-zero when findings at or above this level survive |
| `--no-publish` | skip posting the PR review comment and recording review history |

Examples:

```bash
gx review --scope security                  # security-focused pass over the current changes
gx review --focus src/auth --deep           # deep review of just the auth directory
gx review "did we break the retry contract?"
```

### What gets reviewed

`gx review` picks the change set in this order:

1. `--base <ref>`, when you pass it — the range `<ref>...HEAD`.
2. Your working-tree changes, when there are any. This is the usual case while you work.
3. Otherwise the commits on your branch, `<merge-base>...HEAD` against the base branch it detects (`main`, `master`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`), falling back to the last commit.

So a clean checkout with everything committed still gets reviewed. If there is genuinely nothing to review, `gx review` says so and names the refs it tried — it never reports a clean review of code it did not read.

`gx review` is read-only: it does not require `gx init`, and it never installs hooks or writes GX state into the repository it reviews. You can point it at any checkout, including one you do not own.

### As a CI gate

```bash
gx review --base origin/main --fail-on strong --no-publish --json
```

`--fail-on` takes `none` (the default), `any`, `speculative`, `worth-exploring`, `strong`, or `blocking`. Exit codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | no findings at or above the level |
| `3` | findings at or above the level survived |
| `4` | nothing was reviewed — a gate should not pass without inspecting code |

Pair it with `--no-publish` so a CI run does not post PR comments, and `--json` to parse findings yourself.

## gx auth

```bash
gx auth login                     # sign in through GitHub
gx auth login --name "work-mbp"   # set the machine name shown in the console
gx auth status                    # show current auth state (--json for scripts)
gx auth logout
```

Signs the CLI into GX Cloud through GitHub. Signed-in devices appear in the web app with machine name, GX version, last-used time, and session expiry.

## gx set key

```bash
gx set key                                            # interactive: pick provider, paste key
gx set key --provider anthropic --key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Optional — GX works without a key, and signed-in users get AI features through GX Cloud. Set one when you want GX to call a specific provider or model directly. Stores the key in `~/.gx/inference.json` (or `$GX_HOME/inference.json`); an existing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment is preferred when present. Providers: `anthropic`, `openai`.

## gx doctor

```bash
gx doctor            # diagnose capture, hooks, and the publish queue
gx doctor --fix      # apply safe repairs
gx doctor --json     # machine-readable report
gx doctor --report   # send this diagnosis and recent logs to support
```

Checks local GX state: session capture health, the Git and Claude hooks, the publish upload queue (and retries anything stuck there), and repository workflow state. `--fix` applies the repairs it can make safely.

`--report` uploads the diagnosis together with recent GX logs and prints a report ID and URL — use it when something misbehaves and you want the team to see what happened. It needs GX Cloud: use a released install and `gx auth login`.

## gx version

```bash
gx version
gx version --json   # machine-readable build metadata
```

## Shortcuts

The CLI installer installs `gxr` as a shortcut for `gx review`:

```bash
gxr   # gx review
```

It is a symlink to the same `gx` binary.

## Diagnostics (advanced)

One hidden utility command, for forcing a capture upload out of band:

```bash
gx capture sync   # force a session capture sync
```

Everything else lives on `gx doctor`.

# MCP Setup

The GX MCP server ships with the CLI as a local stdio binary (`gx-mcp`). It shells out to your `gx` binary, so repo state stays on your machine.

## Install GX

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth login
```

That places `gx` and `gx-mcp` in `~/.local/bin`.

If a repo is not initialized, MCP runs `gx init` non-interactively before `gx_review` runs — using Git identity when available, or `GX_MCP_INIT_NAME` / `GX_MCP_INIT_EMAIL`.

## Connect in one command

Use [`add-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/add-mcp) to register GX with the agents on your machine (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, VS Code, and more):

```bash
npx add-mcp "$HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp" \
  --name gx \
  --env "GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx" \
  -g
```

`-g` installs globally so GX is available in every project. Omit it to write project-level config (for example `.cursor/mcp.json`) instead.

Useful flags:

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `-y` | Non-interactive (skip prompts) |
| `-a cursor` | Target a specific agent (repeatable) |
| `--all` | Install to every supported agent |
| `--auto-approve` | Pre-approve tools for Codex / Claude Code |

Most clients only load MCP servers at startup — restart the client or open a new chat after installing.

### Or let `gx init` register

```bash
gx init
```

When supported agent CLIs are on your `PATH`, `gx init` registers GX automatically and reports something like `MCP ok: claude, Cursor`.

## Set up with your agent

Paste this into Claude, Cursor, or any MCP-capable agent:

```text
Help me set up the GX MCP server in this agent.

GX is the quality layer for agent-written code. You keep using plain Git; GX's
hooks record and publish automatically. The CLI installs a local stdio MCP
binary at ~/.local/bin/gx-mcp that exposes one tool, gx_review.

1. If gx isn't installed:
   curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
   then: gx auth login
2. Register the MCP globally with add-mcp:
   npx add-mcp "$HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp" --name gx --env "GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx" -g -y
3. Tell me if I need to restart or open a new chat, then wait.
4. Once tools are available, confirm gx_review shows up, then walk me through
   the save flow — plain Git: git add → git commit → git push. GX's hooks
   record the revision and publish the review bundle; gx_review is there when
   I want AI review.

Docs: https://gx.run/docs/mcp
```

## Use GX through Executor

[Executor](https://executor.sh) is an MCP gateway: point agents at Executor once, then add GX (and other tools) as integrations behind it. Useful when you already route tools through Executor or want shared policy across agents.

GX is a **local stdio** server, so add it from Executor running on the same machine (CLI or desktop). Stdio integrations spawn a subprocess — enable them only in trusted single-user setups.

### From the Executor UI

1. Install GX (see above) and start Executor locally (`executor install` then `executor web`, or the [desktop app](https://executor.sh)).
2. Open **Add Integration** (or **Add Source**).
3. Choose the **stdio** transport.
4. Set:
   - **Command:** `$HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp` (expand to an absolute path if the UI requires it)
   - **Name / namespace:** `gx`
5. Optional: add env var `GX_BINARY` = `$HOME/.local/bin/gx`. If omitted, `gx-mcp` looks for `~/.local/bin/gx`, then `gx` on `PATH`.
6. Save, then confirm the tool appears (search for `gx_review`).

Agents that already talk to Executor pick up GX from the shared catalog — no per-client `gx-mcp` registration needed.

### From the Executor SDK

With stdio MCP allowed on the host:

```ts
import { createExecutor } from "@executor-js/sdk";
import { mcpPlugin } from "@executor-js/plugin-mcp";

const executor = await createExecutor({
  plugins: [mcpPlugin({ dangerouslyAllowStdioMCP: true })] as const,
});

const scope = executor.scopes[0]!.id;

await executor.mcp.addIntegration({
  scope,
  transport: "stdio",
  name: "GX",
  slug: "gx",
  command: `${process.env.HOME}/.local/bin/gx-mcp`,
  env: {
    GX_BINARY: `${process.env.HOME}/.local/bin/gx`,
  },
});
```

`env` here supplies values for the connection (Executor stores them and injects them at launch). See [Executor MCP docs](https://executor.sh/docs/mcp-proxy) and [`@executor-js/plugin-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@executor-js/plugin-mcp).

### Connect your agent to Executor (not GX directly)

If the agent should only speak to Executor:

```bash
# Local HTTP endpoint (port may differ — use the Connect card in the UI)
npx add-mcp http://127.0.0.1:4788/mcp --transport http --name executor -g

# Or stdio, with the executor CLI on PATH
npx add-mcp "executor mcp" --name executor -g
```

Then add GX inside Executor as above.

## Manual registration

Prefer `add-mcp` when you can. These are the per-client equivalents:

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add gx -- env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

### Cursor

```bash
cursor mcp add gx -- env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

### Codex CLI and Codex app

```bash
codex mcp add gx --env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx -- $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

Or edit `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.gx]
command = "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/gx-mcp"

[mcp_servers.gx.env]
GX_BINARY = "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/gx"
```

On Linux, use `/home/YOU/.local/bin/...`.

### Other MCP clients

Same stdio shape:

```bash
env GX_BINARY=$HOME/.local/bin/gx $HOME/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

Example Cursor / Claude `mcp.json` entry:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gx": {
      "command": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/gx-mcp",
      "env": {
        "GX_BINARY": "/Users/YOU/.local/bin/gx"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Tools

| Tool | CLI command | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gx_review` | `gx review [prompt]` | AI review using local and cloud context |

`gx_review` is the only MCP tool. Saving and publishing are plain Git, not MCP calls: `git add` + `git commit` record the revision through GX's hooks, and `git push` captures the session and publishes the review bundle through the pre-push hook. Open the PR with `gh pr create`.

`gx_review` accepts an optional `cwd` (repository working directory; defaults to the MCP server process cwd) and may run up to 5 minutes.

### gx_review

| Parameter | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | string | reviewer prompt, e.g. `"check auth rollback risks"` |
| `scope` | enum | `architecture`, `security`, `performance`, `onboarding`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `testing`, `maintainability` |
| `focus` | string | limit review to files under this path prefix |
| `deep` | boolean | full-spectrum review with more local and indexed context |
| `verbose` | boolean | include repo facts, docs, and changed files |

## Agent workflow

When a user says "save work", "save using gx", or "save with gx", use plain Git — GX's hooks do the GX work automatically:

1. Stage with `git add` (one logical change per revision)
2. `git commit -m "..."` — a hook records it as a GX revision
3. `git push` for ready stacks (unless they ask to keep work local) — the pre-push hook captures the session and publishes the review bundle
4. Open the PR with `gh pr create` — do not seed a `## Summary`; GX Cloud appends it

Run `gx_review` (or the `gx review` CLI) whenever you want AI review of the current change, typically before pushing.

A typical save sequence:

```bash
git add src/backoff.js
git commit -m "add exponential backoff helper"
git push
```

Provenance is inferred automatically: the pre-push hook matches captured sessions to the hunks they changed, so there is nothing for the agent to attach by hand.

GX PR summaries are posted for PRs whose branch was pushed through GX with `git push` while the pre-push hook is installed. A PR opened before that push will not get a summary until the branch is pushed through GX.

## AGENTS.md instructions

`gx init` offers to append these instructions to your repo's `AGENTS.md`. If you skipped that step, add them manually:

```markdown
Version control: plain Git. Once `gx init` installs the hooks, GX records and
publishes automatically — there is no GX save verb.

Default flow:
- Run `git add` to stage the files for this revision.
- Run `git commit -m "..."` to save. A GX hook records the commit as a reviewable revision.
- Run plain `git push` to publish. The GX pre-push hook captures the session and publishes code changes, sessions, and GX metadata to GX Cloud automatically — do not run `gx push` or `gx capture push` yourself; they bypass the hook.
- Open PRs with `gh pr create` (or the GitHub UI). Do not seed a `## Summary` in the PR body — leave human notes only; GX Cloud appends the rich summary below once the PR exists.

For AI review, run the `gx_review` MCP tool (or the `gx review` CLI) on the current change.
```

# Interact with GX in GitHub PRs

GX adds paid review features inside GitHub pull requests.

The CLI records sessions and revisions and publishes them for free. GitHub PR Summaries and `@gx` chat run through GX Cloud and require the paid PR feature set (or an active free trial).

## Prerequisites

1. Sign in with `gx auth login` (or sign in on the console).
2. Install the GX GitHub App on your personal account or organization so GX can post comments and read PR context. From the console, use **Install on GitHub** after the download step (`/install-github`), or open [github.com/apps/satoricorp-gx](https://github.com/apps/satoricorp-gx) directly.
3. Point the GitHub App webhook at the GX Cloud API:

```text
https://api.gx.run/github/webhook
```

4. Publish work through GX (`git push` with the GX pre-push hook). A PR created only in the GitHub UI will not get a GX summary until that branch is pushed through GX with capture metadata present.

## PR Summaries

GX writes one rich PR Summary into the **pull request description** (not a separate comment). Any human description already on the PR stays above the GX block; later regenerations replace only the GX section.

When opening a PR (`gh pr create` or the GitHub UI), leave the body for your own notes — do **not** seed a `## Summary` section. GX Cloud appends the rich summary once the PR exists and publish metadata is available.

The summary is intentionally short. It should tell reviewers:

- what changed
- why it changed
- which files deserve attention first
- which files are mechanical or safe to skim
- what session or agent context is relevant

The goal is to point reviewers to the important parts of the change instead of forcing them to read every line with no context.

### When summaries are generated

GX posts summaries from these paths:

- **GitHub webhook** — on `pull_request` `opened` / `synchronize`, when the branch already has a published GX event
- **After publish** — when plain `git push` (with the GX pre-push hook) has a PR number and the GitHub App is installed

The [`POST /v1/summaries/generate`](/docs/reference/api) API stores a summary in GX Cloud. It does **not** write the PR description by itself.

### When no session was captured

A summary is worth more than the diff because a captured coding session explains it. When no session context reached the summary, GX says so in the PR body rather than letting a diff-only summary pass for a context-rich one:

> *No captured coding session was linked to this branch, so this summary is based on the diff alone. That usually means the branch was pushed without GX's pre-push hook installed, so nothing was captured.*

Install the hooks with `gx init` in the repo (or `gx init --global` once per machine) and push again — the pre-push hook captures the session on the way out. When context is present the note is absent, and the footer reports what informed the summary.

### Trial and paid access

Orgs on the free plan get PR Summaries during a free trial window (default 7 days from org creation, or the entitlement returned by GX Cloud). After the trial ends, summaries require a paid plan. When quota blocks a summary, GX can post an upgrade comment on the PR instead.

## Chat with `@gx`

Mention `@gx` in a PR comment to ask questions about the pull request.

Ask for orientation:

```text
@gx summarize this PR for someone reviewing it cold
@gx which files should I review first?
@gx what is safe to skim?
```

Ask about a specific part of the diff:

```text
@gx explain the auth callback changes
@gx why did the migration file change?
@gx what does this new background job do?
```

Ask for risk or follow-up review:

```text
@gx what is the highest-risk change in this PR?
@gx are there missing tests?
@gx is this related to the previous retry bug?
```

GX answers from available review sources and cites the sources it used. Because published revisions carry session provenance, `@gx` can answer "why" questions — what the author asked for, which commands and tests ran — that a plain diff cannot.

### Override learned rules

You can use `@gx` to retire a learned rule:

```text
@gx skip rule never use var
@gx do not enforce this migration naming rule
```

When a matching active rule exists, GX retires it and records the override. Rule overrides require GitHub **write**, **maintain**, or **admin** permission on the repository. Collaborators without write access are denied.

## Data sources

GX answers from the current PR first: the published GX revision diffs, changed hunks, file paths, PR comments, and the latest PR Summary.

When available, GX can also use captured coding-session context, indexed codebase context, previous findings, learned rules, and git blame history. Current PR changes remain the source of truth for what changed.

## GitHub App

Install from the console (**Install on GitHub**) or at [github.com/apps/satoricorp-gx](https://github.com/apps/satoricorp-gx). To post summaries and replies, GX needs installation-scoped access for the repository. The local CLI can still record and push branches without the paid PR feature set. The paid features are the GitHub-hosted review layer: PR Summaries, `@gx` chat, and cloud-backed review context.

# Troubleshooting

Start with the built-in doctor:

```bash
gx doctor          # diagnose capture, hooks, and the publish queue
gx doctor --fix    # apply safe repairs automatically
```

If something still misbehaves, `gx doctor --report` uploads the diagnosis and recent GX logs to support and prints a report ID you can share.

## Common errors

### Nothing staged to commit

A GX revision follows your staged index, so stage the changes you want in it before committing:

```bash
git add <files>     # or git add -p to select hunks
git commit -m "describe this change"
```

With an empty index there is nothing for the commit hook to record — stage your changes first.

### `Run gx init first.`

The repository has no GX identity yet. Initialize it once:

```bash
gx init        # interactive
gx init -y     # accept defaults, for scripts and agent sandboxes
```

### Push reports remote divergence

The remote moved since you last fetched — a branch was merged, closed, or force-pushed. Bring your local branch up to date, then push again:

```bash
git pull --rebase
git push
```

### `Could not upload GX review context ... GX Cloud is not configured`

The push of Git refs succeeded, but the session/metadata upload was skipped because the CLI has no cloud endpoint. Released installs have the endpoint baked in, so this usually means a from-source build — set `GX_CLOUD_URL` or reinstall the released CLI:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
gx auth status || gx auth login
```

Local remote metadata is still recorded, so nothing is lost. Queued uploads are drained on the next `git push`.

### `gx-mcp not found; install GX CLI package first`

`gx init` tried to register the MCP server but could not find the `gx-mcp` binary. Reinstall the CLI package, which places both binaries in `~/.local/bin`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://download.gx.run/install.sh | sh
```

Then re-run `gx init`, or register manually per [MCP setup](/docs/mcp).

### No PR Summary appeared on my pull request

Check, in order:

1. The branch was pushed with `git push` while the GX pre-push hook is installed. A PR created only in the GitHub UI has no capture metadata.
2. The GX GitHub App is installed on the repository, with the webhook pointed at `https://api.gx.run/github/webhook`.
3. Your org's trial window or paid plan is active — when quota blocks a summary, GX posts an upgrade comment instead. See [Pull Requests](/docs/github).

### Sessions are not being captured

`gx init` installs the capture hooks (Git pre-push, Claude Code `Stop`/`SessionEnd`). Verify and repair:

```bash
gx doctor          # shows capture and hook state
gx doctor --fix
```

## Environment

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `GX_HOME` | override GX's state directory (default `~/.gx`) — inference key, capture data, workspaces |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` | model credentials for local inference; `gx set key` stores one persistently |
| `GX_BINARY` | path to the `gx` binary the MCP server should run |
| `GX_MCP_INIT_NAME` / `GX_MCP_INIT_EMAIL` | identity for MCP's non-interactive `gx init` |

## Uninstall

```bash
rm -f ~/.local/bin/gx ~/.local/bin/gxr ~/.local/bin/gx-mcp
```

This removes the installed binaries only. Local GX data remains in `~/.gx`; delete that directory too if you want a clean slate. Your Git repositories are untouched — everything GX published is ordinary Git.

## Send logs to support

```bash
gx doctor --report
```

Runs the diagnosis and uploads it with recent GX logs (requires `gx auth login`), then prints a report ID and URL to share with the team.

# Changelog

Breaking changes land here first. Subscribe to the repo or check back before upgrading.

## July 2026 — GX is no longer a Git porcelain

GX now does one thing: capture your coding sessions and make review great. You work in
plain Git; GX's surface is `gx init` (hooks), `gx review` (AI review), and PR Summaries.
This shipped as a series of CLI releases in July 2026.

### Removed CLI commands

`gx commit`, `gx status`, `gx push`, `gx edit`, `gx base`, `gx generate`, and `gx sync`
have been removed. Use plain Git instead:

| You used to run | Now run |
| --- | --- |
| `gx commit` | `git commit` |
| `gx status` | `git status` |
| `gx push` | `git push` |
| `gx sync` | `git fetch` / `git pull` — GX publishes automatically on push |

Capture is unaffected: the hooks installed by `gx init` record revisions on `git commit`
and publish sessions on `git push`. Uploads that fail retry automatically on your next
push, and `gx doctor` can retry them on demand.

### Removed ambient capture (LaunchAgent)

The background capture service (`gx ops capture` / the GX LaunchAgent) is removed.
Session capture is transcript-based via the hooks `gx init` installs — nothing runs in
the background anymore. Upgraded CLIs remove an existing LaunchAgent automatically the
next time `gx init` runs; you can also remove it manually from `~/Library/LaunchAgents`.

### A smaller command surface

`gx demo` and the hidden `gx ops` tree are removed, and `gx report` folded into
`gx doctor --report` (the old `gx report` still works as a hidden alias for one
release). What remains: `gx init`, `gx review` (alias `gxr`), `gx auth`, `gx set`,
`gx doctor`, and `gx version`.

### MCP server exposes `gx_review` only

The MCP tools `gx_commit`, `gx_status`, `gx_push`, `gx_publish`, and `gx_edit` were
removed along with the porcelain. Agent configurations that reference them should call
plain Git commands instead; review stays available as the `gx_review` tool.

### Publish API: bundle schema v2

`POST /v1/publish` bundles are now `schema_version: 2`: the `stack` array and the
jj-era `change.jj_change_id` field are gone, replaced by a flat `revisions` list
(commit, `GX:` trailer ID, description, files, branch, base branch, patch). Version 1
bundles remain accepted, so older CLIs keep working during the transition — but
upgrade to keep PR Summaries at full quality.

### `GET /bookmarks` is now `GET /v1/reviews`

"Bookmark" was jj's word for a branch, and the row it returns is really one review per
pull request. The endpoint is now `GET /v1/reviews`. `GET /bookmarks` still works and
returns an identical response — it forwards to the new path and sets a `Deprecation`
header — so nothing breaks today. Point integrations at `/v1/reviews`; the old path
will be removed once traffic to it stops.

### Session retention

Captured sessions are staged locally as lightweight references and published on
`git push`; published sessions are kept with your review history in GX Cloud. Earlier
docs described a 30-day local retention window — that description was inaccurate and
has been removed.

### Unchanged, and stable going forward

- The `GX: https://gx.run/r/<id>` commit trailer format.
- The PR Summary block and its `<!-- gx:pr-summary:v1 -->` marker — your PR
  description stays above it, GX writes below it.
- `gx init`, `gx init --global`, `gx review`, `gx doctor`, and the capture hooks.

### Discontinued

The GX menu bar app for macOS is discontinued as of July 2026. The CLI hooks replace
everything it did.

# API

GX Cloud APIs use bearer-token authentication.

```bash
export GX_API_URL="https://api.gx.run"
```

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | API and database reachability |
| `GET /v1/auth/me` | inspect the authenticated caller |
| `POST /v1/publish` | publish a GX review bundle (what the pre-push hook sends) |
| `GET /v1/reviews` | list reviews for review surfaces (was `GET /bookmarks`) |
| `GET /v1/review/context` | review context for a repo/ref range |
| `GET /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId` (+ `/plan`, `/decision`) | Console review experience |
| `POST /v1/summaries/generate` | generate and store a PR Summary |
| `POST /github/webhook` | GitHub App webhook (PR Summaries, `@gx` chat) |
| `POST /v1/extracts` | ingest hunk links and push metadata |
| `POST /v1/sessions` | ingest raw captured session content |
| `GET /v1/activity` | recent summaries, sessions, learned rules |
| `POST /v1/code-review-history/record` / `/search` | record and search review findings |
| `POST /v1/reported-logs` | upload CLI logs for support |
| `POST /gx/openai/responses` / `/chat-completions` | OpenAI proxy through GX Cloud |

## Authentication

`requireAuth` accepts these modes:

### GitHub token

For most user-facing integrations:

```bash
gh auth status || gh auth login
export GITHUB_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"
```

If you need to refresh scopes for private repositories:

```bash
gh auth refresh -s read:user -s repo
export GITHUB_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"
```

Attach the token:

```bash
-H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

GX validates GitHub tokens against the GitHub user API and maps the caller to `github:<id>`. You can optionally add `X-Org-Id: $GX_ORG_ID`; otherwise GX resolves a default org.

### CLI session token

After `gx auth login`, the CLI can use a `gxcs_*` session token. The API verifies it through Convex (`CONVEX_SITE_URL` must be configured on the server).

```bash
-H "Authorization: Bearer $GX_CLI_SESSION_TOKEN"
```

### Console service key

The Console BFF authenticates with the shared cloud API key and impersonates a user:

```bash
-H "Authorization: Bearer $GX_CLOUD_API_KEY" \
-H "X-User-Id: $USER_ID" \
-H "X-Org-Id: $GX_ORG_ID"
```

## GET /health

Check that the API and database are reachable.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/health"
```

## GET /v1/auth/me

Inspect the authenticated user, org, token label, CLI session, and machine when available.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

With an explicit org:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/auth/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: $GX_ORG_ID"
```

Response fields include `org_id`, `user_id`, `token_label`, and optional GitHub/session machine fields.

## POST /v1/publish

Publish a GX review bundle. This is what the GX pre-push hook sends on `git push`, after Git has produced branches and commits and GX has captured sessions and review metadata.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/publish" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "event": "gx.pr",
    "schema_version": 2,
    "created_at": 1760000000000,
    "gx_version": "0.0.0",
    "repo": {
      "root_path": "/repo",
      "backend": "git",
      "remote_url": "https://github.com/org/repo.git"
    },
    "push": {
      "branch_name": "feature/example",
      "head_commit_id": "abc123",
      "github_pull_request_url": "https://github.com/org/repo/pull/123"
    },
    "revisions": [],
    "sessions": []
  }'
```

`revisions` carries one entry per commit being published — `revision_id` (the ID from the commit's `GX:` trailer), `commit_id`, `description`, `files`, `branch_name`, `base_branch_name`, and `patch`. `sessions` carries the captured agent sessions with their model, token, and timing metadata. Bundles with `schema_version: 1` (the older `stack`/`change` shape) remain accepted.

The server stores the publish event, upserts a bookmark, indexes artifacts when configured, and returns review/bookmark metadata. When a PR number is present and the GitHub App is installed, publish may also post a missing PR Summary.

Without `event: "gx.pr"`, the same route accepts a lighter **registration-only** payload (`repo_full_name`, `branch_name`, `head_commit_id`, …) to upsert bookmark metadata.

## GET /v1/reviews

List reviews for review surfaces, newest first. One review is one branch's published work — the PR it becomes, the latest publish event, and its plan status.

Query parameters: `merge_status` (`open`, `merged`, or `closed`; any other value is a `400`) and `repo_full_name`. Both optional.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/reviews?merge_status=open" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

Filter to one repository:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/reviews?repo_full_name=org/repo&merge_status=open" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

<Note>
  `GET /bookmarks` is the former name of this endpoint and still works — it forwards to
  `/v1/reviews` and returns exactly the same response, with a `Deprecation` header. Move
  to `/v1/reviews`; the old path will be removed in a future release.
</Note>

Response: an array of reviews.

```json
[
  {
    "id": "bm_123",
    "repo_full_name": "org/repo",
    "branch_name": "feature/retry-backoff",
    "title": "Add retry/backoff utilities",
    "revision": 3,
    "head_commit_id": "ae0d5b62...",
    "remote_head_sha": "ae0d5b62...",
    "merge_status": "open",
    "updated_at_ms": 1760000000000
  }
]
```

## GET /v1/review/context

Fetch review context for a repo/ref range. The response can include rules, collision hints, hunk links, and indexed snippets.

```bash
curl --get "$GX_API_URL/v1/review/context" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "repoRoot=/repo" \
  --data-urlencode "base=main" \
  --data-urlencode "head=HEAD"
```

## Console review experience

These routes power the Console review UI. They require auth like other `/v1` routes.

### GET /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId

Load the full review experience for a bookmark (plan, usage, changes, summary, activity).

### POST /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId/plan

Generate or regenerate a review plan for the bookmark.

### POST /v1/reviews/:bookmarkId/decision

Record an approve/merge decision. Passing `merged: true` updates bookmark `merge_status`.

## POST /v1/summaries/generate

Generate a PR Summary for a bookmark or event and **store it in GX Cloud**. This endpoint does not post the comment to GitHub; GitHub posting is driven by the webhook and publish paths. See [GitHub PRs](/docs/github).

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/summaries/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bookmarkId":"..."}'
```

Or generate from an event:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/summaries/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"eventId":"..."}'
```

PR Summary and GitHub PR chat features are paid GX Cloud features (with a free-trial window).

## POST /github/webhook

GitHub App webhook endpoint for PR Summaries and `@gx` chat.

```text
POST https://api.gx.run/github/webhook
```

Authenticated with `X-Hub-Signature-256`, not a bearer token. Configure this URL on the GitHub App.

## POST /v1/extracts

Ingest hunk links and push metadata.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/extracts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repoRoot": "/repo",
    "refRange": "main..HEAD",
    "headCommit": "abc123",
    "gxVersion": "0.0.0",
    "hunkLinks": [
      {
        "hunkID": "src/app.ts:10-20",
        "file": "src/app.ts",
        "lineStart": 10,
        "lineEnd": 20,
        "tier": 1,
        "confidence": 0.91,
        "authorship": "agent",
        "tool": "codex",
        "model": "gpt-5"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## POST /v1/sessions

Ingest raw captured session content.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "sessionId": "session-123",
    "tool": "codex",
    "model": "gpt-5",
    "content": "redacted transcript text",
    "capturedAtMs": 1760000000000
  }'
```

## GET /v1/activity

Read recent summaries, sessions, and learned rules. `limit` accepts 1–100 (default 20); page with the returned `nextCursor`.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/activity?limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

With pagination:

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/activity?limit=20&cursor=$CURSOR" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN"
```

Response shape: `{ items, limit, nextCursor }`.

## POST /v1/code-review-history/record

Record review findings so future reviews can retrieve previous decisions and patterns.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/code-review-history/record" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repoFullName": "org/repo",
    "repoRootPath": "/repo",
    "branchName": "feature/example",
    "headCommitId": "abc123",
    "sourceKind": "manual",
    "prompt": "review auth changes",
    "summaryText": "Auth review completed",
    "findings": [
      {
        "title": "Missing validation",
        "summary": "The handler accepts an unchecked token.",
        "filePath": "src/auth.ts",
        "lineStart": 42,
        "severity": "medium",
        "confidence": 0.8
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## POST /v1/code-review-history/search

Search prior review findings for a repo.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/code-review-history/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "repoFullName": "org/repo",
    "query": "auth validation",
    "filePaths": ["src/auth.ts"],
    "limit": 5
  }'
```

## POST /v1/reported-logs

Upload reported CLI logs for support.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/v1/reported-logs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "gx_version": "0.0.0",
    "os": "darwin",
    "arch": "arm64",
    "repo_root": "/repo",
    "repo_full_name": "org/repo",
    "error": "publish failed",
    "logs": [
      {
        "path": "publish.log",
        "content": "redacted log content"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## POST /gx/openai/responses

Proxy a valid OpenAI Responses API request through GX Cloud.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/gx/openai/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-5",
    "instructions": "Be concise.",
    "input": "Summarize this change."
  }'
```

## POST /gx/openai/chat-completions

Proxy a valid OpenAI Chat Completions request through GX Cloud.

```bash
curl "$GX_API_URL/gx/openai/chat-completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "Summarize this change." }
    ]
  }'
```
